## Task statement

**Invariant.** No secret in source/history; non-dev env never boots on a default; credential files are 0600

**Oracle.** secret scanners; startup under `APP_ENV=staging/prod`; `stat`

**Violation cases seeded.** hardcoded key; dev default reachable in staging; 0644 session file

Source: `EVALS-PLAN.md` Layer 0.

## Construction

Every task is a directory `evals/cases/P5/<case>/` holding a `case.yaml` (the task record: `id`, `property`, `origin`, `grader`, `expect`, `description`, `canary`), a `vuln/` tree with exactly one planted violation, and a `clean/` twin — the same code with the violation fixed through the toolkit primitive. The grader scores both: the violation must be detected in `vuln/` (recall) and not in `clean/` (precision), so the clean twin is the baseline scored alongside every task.

Origins, in the priority order of EVALS-PLAN.md Layer 2:

- **historical-miss** (2): a real miss from this program, encoded permanently.
- **derived** (3): a violation case from the Layer 0 row, in a code shape the historical cases do not already cover.

| task | origin | grader | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `P5-debug-from-not-production-01` | derived | `secrets_boot` | smart-dispatch settings: DEBUG derived from `not is_production()`, and the secret default keyed off DEBUG, so a staging box ran with DEBUG on and the development key. Settings-class shape. clean derives DEBUG from is_dev() and the key from require_secret. |
| `P5-env-fail-open-staging-01` | historical-miss | `secrets_boot` | toolkit PR #4: require_secret returned the dev default whenever APP_ENV was not literally prod/production, so staging, qa, prd, live and typos ("prod ", "produciton") all booted on the placeholder key. vuln is that predicate; clean uses require_secret, which allows a default only for an explicit development/test label and fails closed otherwise. |
| `P5-hardcoded-secret-01` | derived | `semgrep` | A credential literal in source; clean reads it from the environment. |
| `P5-session-file-mode-01` | historical-miss | `secrets_mode` | study-hub: the browser storage state (cookies) was written with a plain open(), so it took the process umask and landed 0644. clean writes it through write_private (0600, atomic, umask-independent). |
| `P5-session-file-mode-02` | derived | `secrets_mode` | Same flaw through pathlib in a store class: Path.write_text creates the credential file with the umask default. clean routes the store's save through write_private. |

## Metrics and current numbers

- **recall** = tasks whose `vuln/` the grader detected ÷ tasks, Wilson 95% CI.
- **precision** = tasks whose `clean/` the grader did not flag ÷ tasks, Wilson 95% CI.
- with `--trials K > 1`: **pass@k** (any of k) and **pass^k** (all of k) over tasks.

## Known limitations

From the grader docstrings (what each oracle can and cannot decide):

### `secrets_boot`

> P5 secrets graders (plugin): the two oracles a scanner cannot be.
>
> secrets_boot  expect: {module: settings, secret: API_KEY,
>                        envs: [staging, qa, "prod ", produciton]}
>     Imports `<module>.py` from the variant directory in a fresh subprocess
>     with APP_ENV set to each label and the secret UNSET. Detected = the
>     module boots (exit 0) on a default under any non-development label.
>     Two sanity runs guard the verdict: the module must boot under
>     APP_ENV=dev, and must boot under APP_ENV=staging once the secret is
>     set — otherwise the module is broken, not clean, and the grader errors.
>
> secrets_mode  expect: {target: "session:write_session"}
>     Calls `fn(path, data)` in a temp dir under umask 022 and stats the
>     result. Detected = any group/other permission bit is set.

### `secrets_mode`

> P5 secrets graders (plugin): the two oracles a scanner cannot be.
>
> secrets_boot  expect: {module: settings, secret: API_KEY,
>                        envs: [staging, qa, "prod ", produciton]}
>     Imports `<module>.py` from the variant directory in a fresh subprocess
>     with APP_ENV set to each label and the secret UNSET. Detected = the
>     module boots (exit 0) on a default under any non-development label.
>     Two sanity runs guard the verdict: the module must boot under
>     APP_ENV=dev, and must boot under APP_ENV=staging once the secret is
>     set — otherwise the module is broken, not clean, and the grader errors.
>
> secrets_mode  expect: {target: "session:write_session"}
>     Calls `fn(path, data)` in a temp dir under umask 022 and stats the
>     result. Detected = any group/other permission bit is set.

### `semgrep`

> P3/P5/P8/P9 static rules. Detected = `expect.rule` fires in the variant.
>
> Pattern-based: a fix the rule does not recognize is a precision gap (the first
> P8 sink rule flagged `harden()` inline in an f-string), and a vulnerable shape
> the rule has no pattern for is a recall gap — only the shapes in the corpus are
> known covered. Needs the `semgrep` binary; errors (never passes) without it.

## Contamination policy

- **Canary.** Every `case.yaml`, every registry entry and `tasks.jsonl` carry the string in `evals/registry/CANARY.txt` (BIG-bench convention): a model that can reproduce it has seen this corpus in training, and its scores on it do not measure the property.
- **Split.** This eval is `split: build`. Build-split cases are used to tune rules and defenses. The held-out split (`evals/heldout/`, EVALS-PLAN.md Phase 4) is sealed: written after the defenses, never used for tuning, and scored only in reports.
- **No model in the loop.** Every grader is deterministic code; no LLM judges a result, so there is nothing to contaminate on the grading side.
